Introduction:
We are Founders.

We welcome parents to discover a path of proven success for their children to and through Chicago Public Schools, college, and career.

We empower children to explore our dynamic city and a world of opportunities celebrating who each of them are and becoming individually.

We support one another in creating differentiated world-class instruction every day tailored to each child's unique heart and talents.

We use our credentials and research to draw our path forward.

AlertMessage:
New Approach to Supporting Student Development
Chicago Public Schools (CPS) is reimagining our approach to accountability, emphasizing the holistic development of students. This means focusing not only on academic success but also on students' growth and well-being. We are working hard to fully implement our new approach by Fall 2025. This will be done in stages to give our schools and stakeholders time to understand changes and receive ongoing support. For more information, visit cps.edu/CIDT.
OverallRatingDescription: Per Chicago Board of Education policy, district-managed schools are assigned an annual school accountability status in order to identify schools on remediation or probation.
StudentGrowthDescription: Student Growth measures the change in standardized test scores between two points in time. This growth is compared to the average national growth for schools that started in the same place. A 50th percentile score means the school grew at the same rate as the national average.
PrekSchoolSummary: Our preschool program boosts academic skills through a play-based and inquiry-based approach which helps foster independence, prepares students for kindergarten, and instills a lifelong love of learning. Teachers utilize a district-wide curriculum, the Creative Curriculum, to provide support for student learning and development across all essential areas including social emotional skills. To ensure all students have the opportunity to engage in high-quality early learning experiences, preschool programs are offered free of charge.

Introduction: Catalpa Early Childhood Center is a Chicago Public School Preschool located in the Jefferson Park neighborhood. We offer full day preschool programs for four year olds from 9am-4pm throughout the city of Chicago. Join the Catalpa ECC Community by completing the application on the Chicago Early Learning Site.

Introduction:
We are Santiago: A Personalized Learning school in the heart of Humboldt Park. Under new management by Chicago Public Schools, Esmeralda Santiago Elementary school has the best of both worlds: a small, tight-knit community feel, while open to all students across Chicago. 

Santiago offers:

- Personalized learning curriculum and structures

- Bilingual and ESL services at all grade levels (Spanish/English)

- Robust community partnerships

- High levels of parent involvement and student voice

Introduction:
Chicago Arts High School develops the next generation of diverse, artistically promising scholar-artists through intensive pre-professional training in the arts combined with a comprehensive college preparatory curriculum.

Chicago Arts High School is Chicago's first and only tuition-free, pre-professional arts conservatory high school. At ChicagoArts, students have the unique opportunity to study with working professionals in our five arts conservatories: Creative Writing, Dance, Music, Theatre, and Visual Arts.

Introduction:
Acero Brighton Park, opened in 2013, serves nearly 535 students from kindergarten to eighth grade. 

Our goal at Acero Brighton Park is to immerse scholars in a creative, culturally-diverse reading development program that extends to our other core content classes, all while remaining focused on our care for culture and community. We focus on cracking the reading code in our K-3 classrooms before transitioning to our 4-8 ELA program that immerses our older students in novel study units that focus on complex characters across various genres. 

Brighton Park prides itself on a rigorous curriculum, an individualized approach to learning and strong parent partnerships. In addition to basketball, flag football, soccer, and volleyball athletic opportunities, scholars may also participate in art club, chess club and additional tutoring programs. Brighton Park also prioritizes 8 annual learning opportunities out of the core curriculum, including a unique Ozark Science Camp opportunity for 4th grade scholars in Arkansas.

Recognizing that literacy development is a key component of academic progress, Brighton Park hosts a family event each quarter to promote parents’ engagement in their child’s literacy and math development that connects parents to the school community. We also showcase our creative arts program with an annual Art and Music Showcase in the spring.

Brighton Park is part of the Acero Schools network. At Acero Schools, our mission is transforming minds through academic empowerment and success. We provide a strong academic foundation for students at the elementary level to help them master the fundamental skills necessary for success in high school and beyond.

SchoolLongName: Acero Charter Schools - SPC Daniel Zizumbo
Introduction:
Zizumbo is a charter school that is proud that parents make a thoughtful choice to have their child attend our school. Choice holds us accountable to families that entrust their children to the school.   Zizumbo, our school’s core values are threefold:  Community–we pursue diversity and unity across the student body, faculty, neighborhood partners, and families.  Growth–academic and social growth that is measurable and with measurable data goals.  Joy–-we aim to provide experiences for both students and teachers to experience joy every day at school and work.   

Zizumbo, which opened in 2008, serves more than 570 students from kindergarten to eighth grade. The principal and assistant principal have led the school since its inception. The school is ranked as the #2 Elementary Charter School in Illinois for 2021 by U.S. News and World Report.  The school has earned a Level 1/1+ SQRP since the rating system began.  More than 50% of the faculty has a Master’s Degree or an English Learner/Bilingual endorsement.  Zizumbo features a robust after school program, including the school’s partnership with the Boys and Girls Club of Illinois.

Zizumbo is part of the Acero Schools network. At Acero Schools, our mission is transforming minds through academic empowerment and success. We provide a strong academic foundation for students at the elementary level to help them master the fundamental skills necessary for success in high school and beyond.

Introduction:
Clemente creates a sense of heritage and community that is reflected as a center of public pride. Clemente scholars grow, learn and excel in their students while developing social and emotional skills that will last them a lifetime. 

Opened in 2012, Clemente serves approximately 490 students from kindergarten to eighth grade. Clemente prides itself on a rigorous curriculum, an individualized approach to learning, and strong parent partnerships.  A tradition of excellence is the cornerstone of Clemente, which is driven by the commitment of families and the community.

While rigorous academics are a top priority at Clemente, we also know that social-emotional development and personal growth are important to the overall education of our Lion student body. Our students start each day with a healthy breakfast and social-emotional learning to feed their bodies and minds. After school, there are extensive clubs, activities and sports that involve nearly the entire school.

Clemente’s inspiring teachers, staff, and administrators believe the greatest service we can provide our students is an education that equips them with the intellectual, emotional and social skills necessary to succeed in their post-elementary life.

Clemente is part of the Acero Schools network. At Acero Schools, our mission is transforming minds through academic empowerment and success. We provide a strong academic foundation for students at the elementary level to help them master the fundamental skills necessary for success in high school and beyond.

Introduction:
Legacy Charter School is a public charter school educating approximately 468 scholars in Kindergarten through 8th gr. in Chicago's North Lawndale neighborhood. Legacy is an outstanding center for teaching and learning for children and their families that recognizes and nurtures the full potential of every child, provides a foundation for a college education, and educates its scholars to be creative and critical thinkers and responsible citizens in school, at home, and in the broader community.


Legacy prepares its scholars for success in college and beyond, helping them build a robust academic intellectual foundation from which to grow. Beginning with full-day pre-k, and consistently through 8th gr. Legacy's curriculum emphasizes literacy, and sets the stage for sustainable academic achievement by its scholars. Our curriculum and culture emphasize both academic achievement and social-emotional growth.

Legacy's curriculum educates the whole child. All scholars participate weekly in art, music, and physical education. Team sports and after school clubs are available to scholars, including tutoring, clubs,  basketball, and the Boys & Girls Club.

Introduction:
At Gary Comer College Prep 6-12, we believe every student deserves access to an excellent education that opens doors, regardless of background, zip code, or starting point. Our mission is to develop independent thinkers, courageous problem solvers, and compassionate leaders prepared to thrive in middle school, high school, college, and careers. We envision a future where our alumni are competitive in the workforce, living choice-filled lives, and are agents of positive change in their communities.

Our Priorities for SY26-28: For the next three years, our work will be guided by three driving priorities- undergirded by a culture of clarity, consistency, and connection (C3)

1. Academic Excellence with Equity -- Ensuring all students, especially those furthest from opportunity, have access to rigorous, high-quality instruction and support.

UIC College Prep prepares and empowers students to use their college degrees and careers to make a positive multi-generational change. Our goal is to prove a new possible and close the achievement gap with attention to results and a growth mindset. Introduction:
We partner with families and community stakeholders to cultivate a web of support for students that clears a path to and through college. The mission of North Lawndale College Preparatory Charter High School is to prepare young people from under-resourced communities for graduation from high school with the academic skills and personal resilience necessary for successful completion of college.

Students enrolled in North Lawndale College Prep have an opportunity to be a part of the Phoenix Pact. The Phoenix Pact is a program that makes it possible for graduates of NLCP to go to college where they are most likely to succeed, rather than having to settle for colleges they can afford. The Phoenix Pact awards scholarships so students can go to college with no out-of-pocket cost, it secures grants to limit loan debt and provides counselor support while in college.

Introduction: Muchin College Prep opened in August of 2009 on the 7th floor of a high-rise building downtown. We have consistently ranked among the top 10 highest performing non-selective high schools in Chicago. Our scholars come to Muchin from more than 50 zip codes across Chicago and commute primarily by public transportation to our downtown campus. In addition, our diverse staff represents every region in the US and eight countries outside the US, and includes 15+ year veterans, Ivy League graduates, and NCAA athletes. Our scholars engage in a rigorous curriculum that prepares them for success in college and beyond. In addition to our rigorous curriculum, we focus on character education. We leverage our unique location to provide a variety of opportunities for our scholars to interact with professionals through internships, youth employment, and enriching activities. Since opening, 100% of our scholars have been accepted to two- and four-year colleges and universities. Now in our ninth year of operation, our founding class has seen its first college graduates! We have more than 67% of our first-generation college scholars on track to graduate - outpacing the CPS college completion average.

Introduction:
Perspectives Rodney D. Joslin campus provides a holistic approach to education, combining rigorous college preparatory curriculum with strong social emotional learning to prepare our students for college and for life. Located in South Loop, Joslin serves students from across the city in grades 6-12.

Joslin utilizes our city as a classroom to provide real world and experiential learning opportunities. Joslin’s vibrant, small-school learning environment allows students to build on their educational experience through internships and electives like art, humanities, and STEM courses. AP classes are available and Dual Enrollment is offered in partnership with City Colleges. Joslin provides the foundation for developing ethical leaders prepared for the 21st century.

Our Joslin campus also serves students grades 6-8 at this campus. Our middle schools teach through personalized learning, combining tailored classroom instruction with an online curriculum called Summit, which allows students to work at their own pace and receive personalized instruction based on where they’re at.

To apply for a middle school seat, please visit https://pcsedu.org/enroll/choosing-your-campus/.

We show up each day with a relentless focus on meeting students’ individual needs and modeling just how much they mean to us everyday. 

You belong here – Go Panthers!

–Dr. Jeralyn Harris, Principal of CICS Longwood High School

Introduction:
About the school

Chicago Math and Science Academy (CMSA) is Where Excellence Thrives. CMSA has been rated as Level1 school by Chicago Public School for 8 years in a row. We are a public charter school serving Chicago students in grades 6-12. Our school is located in Rogers Park and most of our students walk to school. CMSA is a diverse community with over 40 countries represented in our school community.

Since 2004, our mission has been to change the trajectory of our students’ lives by providing a rigorous, STEM focused (science, technology, engineering, and math) curriculum while creating an effective, equitable learning community with high 185 days of instruction.

* 90-minute math and reading classes * Project Lead the Way Pre-Engineering Courses * AP College Prep Program * Award winning robotics program

Community and parent engagement

We see parents and the community as partners in our students’ education. We believe that forging strong relationships benefit students and the community.

For further information please visit our website at cmsaonline.net

Introduction:
Perspectives/IIT Math & Science Academy (MSA) prepares our students for success in college and in life by pairing strong social emotional learning with a rigorous college preparatory curriculum that emphasizes science, technology, math & engineering. Located in Bronzeville, MSA serves approximately 500 students in grades 6-12.

MSA offers cutting edge technology that allows students to gain certifications in web design, coding, Adobe Photoshop™, robotics, and relevant STEM courses. Students can also earn college credits through dual enrollment partnerships with City Colleges.

MSA partners with leading organizations, including Horizon Pharma and AAR, to give students mentorship opportunities in STEM industries. We offer over 50 after-school programs and athletic teams.

We also serve grades 6-8 at this campus. Our middle schools teach through personalized learning, combining tailored classroom instruction with an online curriculum called Summit, which allows students to work at their pace, track their work and receive personalized instruction.

To apply for a middle school seat, please visit https://pcsedu.org/enroll/choosing-your-campus/.

Introduction:
Nate Lowry has spent his entire career working in K-12 education as a teacher, leader, coach, and principal. He is thrilled to join the Baker bobcats as the campus principal and is excited to ensure that Baker College Prep lives up to its promise of ensuring all scholars are valued members of a community where they are physically, mentally, and emotionally safe and experience rigorous and relevant curriculum and instruction.

In his most recent role as Chief Academic Officer of the Academies of Math and Science, Nate managed the Schools and Academic Teams, leading the network to be the largest, highest-performing charter in the state of Arizona serving predominantly low-income students. Prior to his time at AMS, he worked as Executive Director for IDEA Greater Austin, where he oversaw 16 schools serving almost 10,000 students. During his tenure as a campus principal, Nate led IDEA Montopolis College Preparatory to be the only school in east Austin to earn a TEA A Rating in 2018.

Nate is a proud Cornell University graduate, and also holds a Master’s Degree in Educational Leadership from Columbia. He strongly believes in holding all students and adults to high expectations while also practicing empathy, and is focused on finding innovative programming that closes the experience gap for all students. When he’s not working you’ll find him traveling, spending time with friends and family, and working out.

Introduction:
Victoria Soto High School, which opened in 2013, serves more than 550 students from ninth through twelfth grade. The school is deeply committed to preparing students for their future through a comprehensive and personalized approach to learning. With the support of a dedicated college counselor, students engage in a wide variety of classes, including honors and AP courses, while leveraging the Gradient Learning Platform, which focuses on whole-student outcomes and social-emotional learning. Soto emphasizes a holistic educational experience, tailoring instruction to meet the unique needs and aspirations of each individual.  

At Soto, students are empowered to pursue their passions, develop their talents, and craft personalized post-secondary plans. By integrating social-emotional support into academics, students build the resilience, character, and intellect necessary for success. All students are challenged at levels appropriate to their readiness, ensuring equitable access to a rigorous education.  

Soto is also proud to offer thriving athletics and fine arts programs that provide students with opportunities to explore their interests and excel outside the classroom. Our athletics teams foster teamwork, discipline, and school pride, while our fine arts programs allow students to express their creativity through visual arts and music.

In addition to academic rigor and extracurricular offerings, Soto is committed to service and community engagement, requiring all students to complete 100 service hours during their high school years. This focus on community involvement complements our mission to prepare students for success in college, careers, and beyond.  

As part of the Acero Schools network, Victoria Soto High School embodies Acero's mission of transforming minds through academic empowerment and success. Our aim is to provide a strong academic foundation while fostering the social-emotional growth and confidence that students need to thrive in their post-secondary journeys.

Introduction: Sarah E. Goode STEM Academy is an Early College Science, Technology, Engineering, and Math School. Our doors opened during the 2012-2013 school year to 242 freshmen. Our mission is for our student "innovators" to earn both a high school diploma and significant college credits while mastering the Goode Life Habits. Through a unique collaboration that connects high school, college and career, Sarah E. Goode STEM Academy partners with IBM and Daley College to develop Innovators that will advance humanity. At Goode STEM Academy, our Innovators DO college. Innovators only take 4 classes each semester and have the opportunity to earn 8 credits above the graduation requirement. In addition, Innovators that meet our college requirements start to take courses at Daley College. Currently, 40% of our sophomores and juniors take classes at Daley College. Our course sequences are aligned to various Associate Degree pathways in Information Technology: computer science, web development, and networking.  In addition, Innovators have the opportunity to intern at various IT corporations throughout Chicago.

SchoolLongName: Consuella B York Alternative High School
Introduction: Welcome to another school year at York High School, where the success of every student matters! As the leader of the school, I'm excited to be accompanied by a team of talented professionals, whose work represents the love of learning and an unyielding servitude to students. Collectively, our core beliefs and values not only reflect a culture of learning, but also one of Care, Productivity and Responsibility; Therefore, we base EVERY decision on what is best for our students. Although we serve in a non-traditional setting, it is my greatest hope that every student finds value in his/her school experience at York. At the end of their tenure here, students should feel empowered to transition with the innermost mind and skill sets that allow competent men and women to bear responsibility for accepting and accessing pathways to productive citizenship. In the words of former Teacher and President (Lyndon B. Johnson), "Nothing matters more to the future of our country than educational opportunity...For freedom is fragile if citizens are ignorant..." The work we do on a day-to-day basis speaks volumes about who we are, and what we believe about the young men and women we unselfishly serve. As you approach the new school year, keep in mind that no part is greater than its whole, and as a school we're only as strong as the supports that we give each other and the educational care that we render to students. I wish you all a productive school year and look forward to another opportunity to serve as your instructional leader.

Introduction: Ombudsman Educational Services provides alternative education programs for high school students who have dropped out or who are at risk of dropping out of school.  A flexible schedule with morning, afternoon, and full time sessions means students don’t have to choose between life and school. Ombudsman offers academic, social and behavioral support so that students earn their high school diplomas and are prepared to make positive choices about the future.  Ombudsman utilizes a number of research-based curriculum resources to deliver its instructional model. Initial and ongoing teacher-led instruction is tailored to ensure each student earns the necessary credits to arrive at graduation in accordance with his or her success plan. Ombudsman’s rigorous and relevant academic programs are accredited by AdvancED and aligned to Common Core and state-specific standards.

Introduction:
My name is Alysha Scott, and I am the proud principal of Chicago Ombudsman West located at 3210 W Roosevelt Road, Chicago, IL 60624. I started at Ombudsman in 2023 as the Assistant Principal and have not only learned what it means to be a leader but have grown personally throughout my experiences at Ombudsman as well. The growth that I have experienced is the same type of growth I want to see in every student that comes to the West campus.

My passion for education stimmed from seeing the systematic differences between education provided in rural/suburban versus urban demographics. It was through that passion that I pursued higher education to obtain my master’s in educational leadership and Family and Human Development with a bachelor’s degree in Sociology.

I am committed to seeing young scholars, the future of our country, be individuals that have the skills and confidence they need to navigate this ever-changing world. I wholeheartedly believe that every student deserves the opportunity to discover and showcase their own passions in life, and that it is my privilege to help them along the way.

Introduction: Ombudsman Educational Services provides alternative education programs for high school students who have dropped out or who are at risk of dropping out of school.  A flexible schedule with morning, afternoon, and full day sessions means students don’t have to choose between life and school. Ombudsman offers academic, social and behavioral support so that students earn their high school diplomas and are prepared to make positive choices about the future.  Ombudsman utilizes a number of research-based curriculum resources to deliver its instructional model. Initial and ongoing teacher-led instruction is tailored to ensure each student earns the necessary credits to arrive at graduation in accordance with his or her success plan. Ombudsman’s rigorous and relevant academic programs are accredited by AdvancED and aligned to Common Core and state-specific standards.

Introduction:
Greetings, Students, Families, and Community Members!

I am honored and excited to welcome you to the Bronzeville Classical School. Thank you for choosing us and embarking on this journey with me.

As a school community, we offer a strong accelerated academic program and we emphasize teaching the whole child. It’s our belief that students should not only develop core academic skills, but they also need to learn how to work in teams, creatively solve problems, learn from mistakes, and pursue goals.

To ensure that our teachers are meeting the individual needs of every student, Bronzeville Classical School will implement a personalized learning approach. We know from both experience and research, that learning styles vary from student to student. We also know that each student brings forth a unique set of skills and interests to the classroom. At Bronzeville Classical School, our teachers have moved away from the “one size fits all” system. Each student is made to feel empowered to develop into curious, self-directed lifelong learners. This will be critical for their success.

To accomplish our mission, and strengthen our school community, we expect parent engagement. You are encouraged to participate as committee members, volunteers and chaperones. Your important voices  shape our school’s climate and culture.

Introduction:
Skinner North has a dedicated, experienced and caring staff.  We are committed to providing rigorous, differentiated instruction to all students.  With a focus on teaching the whole child in an academically advanced environment, we work to establish norms of highly successful and socially-motivated individuals in a community that promotes collaboration, leadership, and celebrates the diversity of the students, families, and staff. 

The school opened in September 2009 and is a selective enrollment school - classsical school that has two classrooms at every grade level from Kindergarten through eighth.  As a classical school, we have an accelerated program (1 year advanced) in literature, mathematics, language arts and the humanities.  Find more about application process at https://www.cps.edu/gocps/elementary-school/explore/selective-enrollment-programs/. Some of our amenities include cooking kitchen, 350-seat auditorium, a learning garden, a library and a gymnasium with a rock climbing wall.

Introduction:
Chicago Tech Academy’s mission is to educate, empower, and connect a diverse next generation of entrepreneurial thinkers to discover their passions, succeed in college and thrive in a digital world.

ChiTech is different because ALL STUDENTS:   

1. Complete hands on projects where they discover, investigate, and solve problems that engage their community through Project Based Learning.   

2. Participate in a college and career success program through Embarc, Senior Seminar, or Genesys Works.   

3. Receive enhanced STEM coursework, with advanced courses in Computer Science, Engineering Design, Principles of Engineering, and Multimedia Arts.   

4. Learn entrepreneurship principles where they are inspired to be fearless, confident, and connected learners. ChiTech also competes in city-wide entrepreneurship challenges.   

5. Engage in real world learning. ChiTech works with 100+ partners such as DDB, Vibes Media, Gogo Air, SAP, TechNexus, Black Tech Mecca and ActiveCampaign to provide students with early exposure to work-based learning and internships.

6. Have the opportunity to participate in a Computer Programming pathway as part of the Career and Technical Education (CTE) Programs; ChiTech is one of only four schools in the city to offer the program.

Introduction:
Gunsaulus Scholastic Academy is a magnet school that combines rigorous academics, arts programming, health and wellness.  The goal of Gunsaulus is to develop students who will shine as learners and leaders in their community and beyond.  The school thrives on the collaboration among staff to create a school where every child's individual needs are met.

Gunsaulus provides enrichment opportunities including high school algebra, band, student council, art, music, and ten different athletic programs. In addition, Gunsaulus supports the whole child through capstone experiences such as camping as well as trips beyond Chicago.  The school also emphasizes a positive environment and has been highlighted as a school within CPS that provides a safe environment for all.

Gunsaulus Scholastic Academy creates an environment that promotes parent engagement and involvement.  The school encourages and welcomes parents to volunteer in classrooms and throughout the school.  Weekly, parents are provided healthy food options through the partnership with the Chicago Food Depository.  In addition, parent classes in literacy and fitness are provided weekly.

Introduction:
Murray Language Academy is a world language magnet school located in Chicago’s historic Hyde Park neighborhood—just steps away from the University of Chicago and the Museum of Science and Industry. At Murray, every student from kindergarten through eighth grade studies a world language—Mandarin, French, or Spanish—building global awareness and cultural appreciation from an early age.

We believe that family involvement is essential to every child’s success. Our families play a key role in shaping the Murray experience both inside and outside the classroom. We’re proud to have an active Parent Teacher Organization (PTO), a dedicated Parent Mentor Program, the Men of Murray group, a Parent Advisory Council (PAC), and a very active Local School Council (LSC). Together, these groups help strengthen our school community through collaboration, service, and advocacy. Whether supporting events like the World Language Fair, Science Fair, Literacy Night, or the End-of-Year Fun Fair, or volunteering in classrooms and committees, Murray parents ensure our school remains vibrant, connected, and deeply rooted in partnership between home and school.

Introduction:
Oscar Mayer Magnet offers Montessori in grades Pre-K through 3rd grade. Pre-K is a full day program for 4 year olds. 

Our intermediate program serves students in grades 4th-5th.  Our goal in the Intermediate Level is to best support all students in the stage between elementary and middle school. We believe our program will provide a comprehensive curriculum, maximum instructional time and unique opportunities for our students. We try to blend the Montessori and IB programs in our classes. At this level, students begin to travel to departmental classes. These classes include writing, science and humanities.

Lastly, we offer the International Baccalaureate (IB) Middle Years Programme (MYP) in Grades 6-8. The International Baccalaureate Middle Years Program (IB MYP) is an internationally recognized education program designed to challenge students to develop the knowledge and skills necessary to participate as active and responsible citizens in a changing world.

All students benefit from taking Music, Art, Spanish, Library, and Physical Education.

PrekSchoolSummary: Our program focuses on the Montessori method of education.  This method is based on the research and practice of Italian physician Maria Montessori. The fundamental principles are that children are innate learners and that they learn best in physical and social settings that permit their natural curiosity to freely develop as they grow. She developed a series of “didactic materials,” or activities based on manipulating objects, that help children to understand abstract concepts by first working in concrete forms. Rather than listening to lectures, students are self-directed and work independently until they have mastered the material. Students are encouraged to assist each other in multi-age classrooms; younger students often learn from older students, and older students learn to lead. These activities provide intellectual stimulation and promote social skills, emotional growth, and physical coordination.

Introduction:
Welcome to Newberry Academy—home of the Bobcats!

At Newberry, our vision is simple and powerful: Leaders Grow Here. Every day, we work to cultivate a positive, safe, and academically rigorous environment where students are empowered to grow—not just as learners, but as whole people and future leaders. Grounded in our mission, we offer mathematically and scientifically integrated opportunities that challenge and nurture every child.

As we look ahead, we’re guided by the words of educator Muriel Summers:

"We only have one chance to prepare students for a world that no one could possibly predict."

That truth shapes everything we do. This year, our theme is Joyful Curiosity—recognizing that students learn best when they are engaged, excited, and yes, even a little messy in their learning. Curiosity often leads to mistakes, but it also leads to discovery, growth, and confidence. We believe that cultivating this joyful spirit is key to helping students take risks, ask questions, and develop into creative, compassionate leaders.

We also know that safety and belonging are the foundations for learning. That’s why this year we are deepening our commitment to restorative practices, ensuring every student, family member, and staff member feels heard, respected, and supported. When we hold space for repair, reflection, and reconnection, we strengthen the relationships that make real learning possible.

Whether you're a returning family or new to our community, we’re excited to partner with you in the journey ahead. At Newberry, we are growing together—with joy, with curiosity, and with a shared belief in the incredible potential of every child.

Joyously yours,
Megan Clendening
Principal, Newberry Academy

Programs.ProgramOverview:
This program provides a comprehensive general education curriculum across all core academic subjects, with a focus on Fine & Performing Arts as an enriching complement to the standard coursework. Arts teachers in Fine & Performing Arts schools work with students and other classroom teachers to provide intensive and integrated instruction in the arts. Students are exposed to various arts opportunities and environments, and have the opportunity to learn and grow in multiple art forms: dance, drama, media arts, music, and/or visual arts.

Technology Program schools thoughtfully integrate technology and digital media throughout the curriculum to ensure that students develop the skills and habits of mind that will enable them to be successful in whatever endeavors they wish to pursue. This includes enabling students to use technology and digital media to demonstrate creative thinking and construct knowledge; communicate and work collaboratively; gather, evaluate and use information; conduct research, manage projects, and solve problems, practice legal and ethical behaviors while online; and understand technology concepts, systems, and operations.

SchoolLongName: Albert R Sabin Elementary Magnet School
Introduction:
Welcome to Sabin Dual Language Magnet School—home of the Sabin Hawks! We are a vibrant PreK–8th grade school proudly serving our community through both a Magnet and a Dual Language program.

At Sabin, we hold high expectations for all students to maximize academic success and social-emotional well-being, with classrooms rooted in love and joy. We see our classrooms as sanctuaries where students feel safe, valued, and inspired to become their best selves.

Our recognized Dual Language program has been celebrated at the district level for consistently preparing students to graduate with the coveted Seal of Biliteracy Honor. We take pride in fostering multilingual and multicultural citizens of the world who are confident in their identities and equipped to lead with compassion.

Sabin is a historic institution with over 110 years of academic excellence. Our small class sizes, deep school culture, robust community partnerships, and championship-caliber sports programming make us a dynamic and supportive place for all learners. We are also proud to offer rich arts-based programming in both music and visual arts, which is deeply embedded into our daily curriculum and extended through our before and after-school programs.

To further support our families, we offer free before and after school programming Monday–Thursday from 8:00 AM to 6:00 PM, rooted in academics, enrichment, arts, sports, and mentorship.

At Sabin, we empower students by cultivating a culturally and linguistically inclusive environment where every student’s identity is honored and celebrated. We are proud to raise the next generation of game-changers and compassionate leaders of our world.

Introduction:
Welcome to Robert A. Black Magnet School, a Leader in Me School, where we are committed to "Building Tomorrow's Leaders." As the proud principal of this prestigious institution, I am honored to serve a community that exemplifies excellence in education, collaboration, and achievement.
Our school is guided by four core values: leadership, equity, rigor, and collaboration. These values shape our approach to fostering an inclusive environment where every student has the opportunity to thrive academically and socially.
At Black, we pride ourselves on delivering instruction that challenges our students to excel. Our curriculum is designed to teach students a grade level above in reading and math, ensuring they are prepared to meet and exceed academic standards. We also offer a specialized gifted middle school science program and provide high school algebra for our 8th graders, ensuring students are equipped with advanced skills that prepare them for future academic success.
Our magnet focus is math and science, and we are dedicated to nurturing curiosity, critical thinking, and innovation in these fields. Through hands-on learning, inquiry-based projects, and collaborative problem-solving, our students develop the skills necessary to excel in a rapidly changing world.
I am incredibly proud to lead a school that values academic excellence, leadership, and strong partnerships with parents, staff, and the broader community. Together, we are creating a supportive environment where students are empowered to become confident leaders, problem solvers, and lifelong learners.

SchoolLongName: Michele Clark Academic Prep Magnet High School
Introduction:
Michele Clark High School: Empowering Excellence in Education

Michele Clark High School, located on Chicago’s Westside, is a premier learning institution dedicated to preparing students to excel in college, careers, and beyond. As an International Baccalaureate (IB), JROTC, Early College, and STEM-focused high school, Michele Clark provides a robust and dynamic educational experience that inspires achievement, leadership, and lifelong learning.

At Michele Clark, students benefit from innovative programs that blend rigorous academic standards with hands-on learning. Through dual credit and dual enrollment opportunities, students can earn college credits while completing their high school studies. The Early College program takes this a step further by offering students the chance to graduate with both a high school diploma and an Associate’s Degree, giving them a significant head start in their academic and professional journeys.

With a curriculum designed to challenge and empower, Michele Clark fosters critical thinking, collaboration, and problem-solving skills. The school’s emphasis on STEM education prepares students for success in technology-driven careers, while the IB program nurtures global awareness and intellectual curiosity. The JROTC program instills discipline, leadership, and a commitment to service, equipping students with essential life skills.

 

Michele Clark High School is more than an academic institution; it is a community that believes in the potential of every student. By combining academic rigor, real-world experiences, and a supportive environment, Michele Clark ensures its students are ready to thrive in college, pursue fulfilling careers, and make a meaningful impact on the world.

Introduction:
MISSION 
Prepare every student comprehensively for their next enriching educational opportunity. 
 
VISION
We will develop the most supportive learning community for the students of Friedrich W. Von Steuben Metropolitan Science Center because everyone deserves the opportunity to realize their potential. 

Von Steuben offers two rigorous programs: Scholars and Magnet College Prep. Scholars is an all-honors, selective program for students who want the challenge of honors and AP-level coursework. The Magnet College Prep Program offers the same coursework as our Scholars Program, with the option to vary the level of classes to meet individual goals. At Von Steuben, we pride ourselves on our students' academic and athletic achievements, providing a well-rounded high school program in a safe, diverse, and enriching atmosphere. Postsecondary goals are supported each year through counselor lessons, college tours, and enrichment activities, including our Von Connection summer program for incoming 9th graders. We offer many athletic, creative, and academic extracurricular activities. Special coursework and programs include Advanced Placement, Dual Credit, Web Design, Gaming, AP Capstone and Pre-Engineering.

Introduction:
Chicago Military Academy at Bronzeville is now an Early College STEM School! Our mission is to prepare cadets for college and post-secondary success through a rigorous and relevant college preparatory curriculum. With the military model providing a culture and structure for social, emotional and academic success, cadets develop leadership and applied academic skills. CMA-B cadets who enter the Academy with drive and self-discipline learn and practice authentic leadership skills that benefit them and their communities for a lifetime.

As an Early College STEM school, CMA-B students will have access to hands-on classes in STEM fields, dual credit/dual enrollment, STEM-based learning outside of the classroom, and STEM career job readiness programs. We are 1:1 technology Academy. The school bridges the rich history of the Bronzeville and the historic 8th Infantry Armory with new renovations, including state-of-the-art science labs.

Marine Leadership is the only one of these programs that is open to students in grades 7-8, and students who enter Marine's program in elementary school are able to continue there for high school without reapplying. Introduction:
Principal's Message

Phoenix Military Academy (PMA) is a college preparatory, STEM high school where cadets are enrolled in the Junior Reserve Officers Training Corps (JROTC). At Phoenix Military Academy (PMA), we are committed to ensuring that all students have access to leadership opportunities and engaging curriculum that will prepare them to be 21st CENTURY LEADERS.

We have incorporated school-wide learning supports that ensure access to a proficiency based, rigorous curriculum that is equitable to all students. The PMA small school setting enables teachers to build personal and positive connections with cadets equipping them for admission to highly selective colleges, successful future career endeavors, and competitive summer opportunities.  PMA cadets become lifelong learners and positive change agents in their communities.

SchoolLongName: Hyman G Rickover Naval Academy High School
Introduction:
Rickover provides a foundation for future success by enabling cadets to excel academically, to engage in meaningful leadership training and to have experiences that prepare them for post-secondary education.

We believe the world is the classroom; examples of the experiences students have are US and international travel, partnership programs with universities, and interaction with US Navy Admirals, political leaders and corporate CEOs. Cadets have opportunities to take Advanced Placement, Dual-Credit, and Dual-Enrollment courses. In the 25-26 school year, Rickover earned a Platinum rating (highest) from the College Board for our success with Advanced Placement. Rickover offers ten advanced placement classes in our small school.

Cadets have opportunities to be peer leaders from their first day of school. They may be responsible for a squad of 5 to a class of 28. They can rise to be responsible for the school of 600 students.

Rickover cadets are part of a tradition of academic excellence and post-secondary preparation. Our graduates for years have averaged over $100,000 in scholarships. 100% of graduates for years have been accepted to a post-secondary school. A large percentage of our graduates complete more than 100 hours of community service.

Our cadets live by our motto Learning to Lead in Order to Serve!

Introduction: Medgar Evers Fine and Performing Arts School offers a standards-based curriculum focused on college, career and civic life. We provide and maintain a climate wherein ALL students can develop intellectually, emotionally, artistically and socially to their fullest potential.  Students have the opportunity to explore their creative abilities by participating in drama, visual arts, dance, band, choir, music, sports and enrichment activities. Through a strong family commitment and partnership between school and community, we strive to develop students that are life-long learners and productive global citizens. We live by our 3 C's, compassion, commitment and champions for children. Partnerships include University of Illinois Urbana, Project Promise, Touch of Wholeness, Children's Literacy Initiative, Forward Momentum Chicago, West Point School of Music, Uniting Voices Choir, Chicago Symphony Orchestra and Raw Talent Performing Arts. Medgar Evers Fine and Performing Arts School will offer children a rigorous, joyful and equitable school experience!

Introduction:
Welcome to W.E.B. DuBois Elementary School!
A Proud World Language School

At DuBois Elementary, we are committed to providing a safe, supportive, and academically challenging environment for all students. As a World Language (Spanish) School, our students build strong language skills and cultural awareness that prepare them to succeed in a global society.

We believe that learning extends beyond the classroom. That’s why we’re proud to partner with organizations like Youth Guidance, Polished Pebbles, Girl Scouts, By the Hand Club, Girls in the Game, and the Altgeld Riverdale Coalition (ARC). These partnerships offer mentorship, leadership development, enrichment activities, and social-emotional learning opportunities that support the whole child.

Family engagement is a vital part of our school’s success. Parents and guardians are encouraged to take active roles through the Local School Council (LSC) and the Parent Advisory Council (PAC). These groups help shape school priorities and strengthen our connection with families.

At DuBois, we are building a strong community where students are empowered to lead, learn, and thrive. We invite you to discover what makes our school a unique environment for children to grow.

Warm regards,
Principal Kelly Flowers

Introduction:
Wacker is a State designated "Commendable" School with a "Gold Circle" Rating for our Pre K programs and a historically rated Tier 1+ neighborhood school that prides itself on being a small, personalized student- centered learning environment. Student skills in reading, writing, listening, and speaking are strengthened by the rigorous curriculum, small group instruction, interventions and enrichment. We are a school of high expectations for all. All classrooms have Interactive Promethean Boards. Student enjoy the use of Chromebooks and IPADs in order to enhance learning. Student voice is valued through our Student Council. Wacker is a recipient of the PLTW (Project Lead The Way) STEM Grant and also the Congressional Arts Grant. Wacker has developed longstanding established partnerships with several community organizations including National CARES Mentoring Program, Invisible Crown Mentoring, Polished Pebbles, Beverly Arts Center, Forward Momentum, Pretty Brown Girls Mentoring Program, Learn Together/Grow Together Day Care Center, South Side Help Center, Free Lunch Academy Social Emotional Learning Group, AARP Tutoring Services, Breaking Bread Male Initiative, Metropolitan Family Services, Ada S. McKinley Family Services, Youth First Counseling Services, Hip Hop Detox Male Mentoring, Chicago State University, St. Xavier University ,Roosevelt University, Urban Gateways, University of Illinois' "Science on the Go", and several other community organizations. Students are encouraged to compete in the African American History Bowl, the School Wide Spelling Bee, the School-Wide Science Fair, along with our Annual "Wacker's Got Talent" Excellence Exhibition. Wacker offers One-to One technology and several, online personalized learning supports, social-emotional learning, and differentiated instruction based upon student needs in order to engage our students.
Parents can participate through the Local School Council and the Title I Parent Advisory Committee(PAC).

SchoolLongName: Thomas J Higgins Elementary Community Academy
Introduction:
Located in the vibrant West Pullman neighborhood on the South Side of Chicago, Thomas J. Higgins Community Academy is a Fine Arts Magnet Academy dedicated to inspiring creativity, curiosity, and a passion for learning. We believe the world is filled with endless possibilities just waiting to be explored, and we strive to equip our students with the tools and mindset to do so. Serving students in grades PK-8, Higgins is committed to our mission: To educate, engage, and enrich. Every child, every day.

At Higgins, our committed educators and staff collaborate to provide a safe, inclusive, and supportive environment where every student can thrive. Through rigorous academics, culturally responsive teaching, and a focus on individualized learning, we foster curiosity, critical thinking, and creativity.

We are proud to offer diverse enrichment opportunities, including unique programs like Braids and Brilliance, the United Voice Choir, and a thriving performing arts partnership with PTDYA. These initiatives celebrate student talents, cultivate self-expression, and provide a platform for students to shine. As a Fine Arts Magnet Academy, we integrate the arts into our curriculum to inspire innovation and a love of learning.

Additionally, Higgins promotes strong family and community partnerships, emphasizing the shared responsibility of fostering student success. With a focus on building confident, compassionate leaders, Higgins Community Academy is a cornerstone of the West Pullman community.

SchoolLongName: Dr. Martin Luther King Jr Academy of Social Justice
Introduction:
Welcome to King Academy. Our school is defined by a commitment to fostering a community where every student can thrive academically and emotionally. Our core values are at the foundation of all that we do: Communication, Respect, Justice, Integrity, Trust, and Excellence.

We embody these values by providing high-quality educational opportunities at every grade level, ensuring our students are prepared to compete successfully with their peers across the district, city, and world. This commitment means providing them with the academic rigor and essential social-emotional support they need to be successful at anything they may encounter during their time here and after.

We educate with an eye on equity and social justice. At King Academy, we ensure that every student knows they have a voice—a voice they must use to advocate not only for themselves but also for their peers, school, and community. We foster partnerships with community organizations to ensure our students use their knowledge, voice, and talent to improve the Englewood community.

All members of the King Academy community believe in the strength of collaboration and teamwork. Here at King #itsaWEthing

Introduction:
Dear Westcott Community,

With immense joy and enthusiasm, I introduce myself as the principal of Westcott Elementary School. My name is Monique Dockery, and I am both honored and excited to continue my role and the tradition of excellence that defines our school.

With a career spanning over three decades in education, I bring a wealth of experience to Westcott. I am committed to creating a world-class, high-quality experience for stakeholders daily along with the staff.

Throughout my career, I have had the opportunity to coach and mentor numerous current leaders within Chicago Public Schools and across Illinois. This experience has reinforced my belief in the importance of a balanced approach to education that respects and integrates the perspectives of all stakeholders, including students, staff, and the broader community.

My philosophy of education is grounded in creating a safe, nurturing environment where every student, staff member, and community member feels valued and supported. I am committed to fostering the whole child, ensuring that academic growth is harmoniously paired with social-emotional development. Our dedicated faculty and staff continuously work diligently throughout the school year to prepare for our scholars. Our curriculum is high quality and aligned with the latest educational standards to move our school forward.

As we embark on this exciting journey together, I look forward to working closely with each of you to continue building a school community that thrives on collaboration, respect, and a shared vision for the future. We will strive to provide our students with the best possible education and a positive, enriching school experience.

SchoolLongName: Orozco Fine Arts & Sciences Elementary School
Introduction:
Orozco Gifted Bilingual Fine Arts and Sciences Academy is a selective enrollment elementary school in Pilsen. We pride ourselves on giving all our students (Pre-K and grades K-8) a well-rounded education with the integration of art, science, and Spanish instruction as well as accelerated and differentiated curricula to support our gifted students.  We serve a diverse community and our academics, facilities, and extracurricular programs reflect that, from athletics and choir to mariachi and gardening.  

Our Mission:  Orozco provides students with an engaging, personalized, and culturally relevant school experience through our Gifted Bilingual instruction and Fine Arts and Sciences program. This includes social-emotional resources and a wide range of extracurricular activities. Orozco works collaboratively among all community members to support students holistically and individually for college and career success.

Our Vision:  Orozco students are part of a rich mosaic in a changing world, inspired to become reflective, innovative, and compassionate leaders through our Gifted, Bilingual, and Fine Arts and Sciences learning.

Introduction:
Leland offers a rigorous daily learning experience for all students in grades PreK - 8th.  Leland is a STEM School that incorporates  CPS S.T.E.M  Curriculum for all K - 8th grade students in our beautiful S.T.E.M. Lab. Students create, observe, and analyze Science, Technology and Math connecting learning to real world problems and solutions. We also offer Digital Arts, Sports opportunities through CPS Score, Dance and Music to ensure that students are well rounded with multiple opportunities to explore, learn and grow. . Leland has been recognized by the U.S. Department of Education as a School of Excellence and a Blue Ribbon School in 2004. Leland is a great place for student experiences where teachers and community supports all learners. We are a community school that offers multiple after school opportunities with Urban Initiative, BUILD, Inc, Project Exploration, and Big Brother Big Sisters of Chicago. There is something at Leland for all students! 
If you're looking for a great place where students can come to learn, participate in different activities in a warm safe creative environment, Leland S.T.EM. is the school for you.

Introduction:
The mission of Brighton Park Elementary is to grow leaders who are engaged, empowered, and educated.  It is our goal for all of our students to leave our school with the foundational tools to serve their community.  

Students who are ENGAGED positively and actively impact their community. 
Students who are EMPOWERED have the intra- and inter-personal skills to participate in their community. 
Students who are EDUCATED possess well-rounded knowledge and skills to contribute to their community.  

We focus on developing leadership skills and helping students find their voice through implementation through the Leader In Me program. Leader in Me is an evidence-based PK-12 model, developed in partnership with educators and designed to designed to build leadership in students, create a high-trust culture, and improve academic achievement

We focus on developing the whole child by:
Teaching leadership to every student.
Creating a culture of student empowerment.
Aligning systems to drive results in academics.

Brighton Park is a Sustainable Community School.  Through this model we offer enriching learning opportunities for parents both in and out of the school day; education and development opportunities for families; and wrap-around supports such as social-emotional wellness.  We use a responsive and restorative approach to supporting both students and families, with multiple opportunities for both students and their families to shape the schools events, programs, and future.  

Our school community operates under four core values:

Rigorous Academics: We believe that engaging students in authentic and challenging academics will develop their critical thinking, problem solving skills, and ensure that they are college and career ready. 

Supportive Environment: We believe that a child’s holistic wellness needs must be met so that they can successfully engage in their academic curriculum and graduate with the tools to become productive and successful members of our community. 

Culturally Responsive and Equitable: We believe that all students are capable of greatness and deserve a high quality education that is inclusive and responsive to their culture, background, and identity. 

Student and Community Centered: We believe that the holistic needs of each student and family should be at the center of everything we do.

Introduction:
Talman Elementary School is a PreK through grade 8 school located in Gage Park Community.  Talman is committed to working with our parents, family, and community partners in developing a safe, supportive, rigorous learning environment. We are focused on addressing the academic, social, and emotional needs of our students.  

The Talman Elementary School Vision is to provide a rigorous and supportive academic environment that includes staff, parents, and community members working together to promote academic achievement with the goal of developing life-long learners.

We envision a safe, rigorous, and academic school environment that embraces cultural diversity; encourages nurturing mutual respect and student ownership. The Talman community strives to expose students to real life learning experiences through the development of a community of disciplined, successful, and independent learners.

The Talman mission is to prepare students for college and career readiness, through rigorous and differentiated planning and instruction aligned to the Common Core State Standards in literacy, mathematics, and all content areas. We recognize that this mission can only be accomplished through fostering strong parent and community partnerships which focus on meeting our students' academic, social, and emotional growth.

The Talman Mission is to provide  high academic standards through real-life, hands-on experiences. These experiences support the development of reading literacy, higher-order thinking skills, and an appreciation for world and life views that empower all students, including English Language Learners and those with special needs, to be life-long learners. By allowing students to take an active role in their education, we enable them to become constructive, contributing members of society.

Introduction:
Irvin C. Mollison IB WORLD School is the Home of the Hawkeyes where we are “Learning Today to become the Leaders of Tomorrow.” The school is named after the first African-American Jurist appointed to the federal bench by the late President Harry S Truman in 1948.  Mollison sits in the heart of Bronzeville just four blocks north of historic 47th St., Harold Washington Cultural Center, and two doors east of Louis Armstrong’s Chicago home where he practiced “scat” with legendary jazz singer, Ella Fitzgerald. Mollison faces the beautiful Martin Luther King Jr. Boulevard and was home to the oldest African American newspaper, the legendary Chicago Defender.  

On average, Mollison welcomes about 220 students and their families. It has a full-day preschool program and full-day kindergarten through 8th-grade classrooms. We are a proud International Baccalaureate school hosting the Middle Years Program. Through our IB program, we offer instruction in both English and Spanish.  

Mollison offers a full range of afterschool activities ranging from academic to extracurricular programs, a boys basketball team, track and field and cross country, soccer, student council, and girls volleyball. We also have partnerships with national and community agencies, businesses, and individuals willing to lend their time and talent to support our students.   At Mollison, we are proud to have an involved and supportive Local School Council and a host of parents who regularly volunteer to support the success of Mollison.  Most importantly, Mollison School is filled with children who have dreams, and their dreams are filled with becoming future leaders and global citizens.

Introduction:
Henry O. Tanner is a community of stakeholders engaging students in meaningful learning experiences to produce college and career ready scholars.    

Tanner school offers 21st Century learning through individualized learning tracks, 1:1 technology integration and digital curriculum implementation. We cultivate and nurture students’ talents and interest through fine and performing arts opportunities and year-round sports programming.   Most recently, Tanner is a recipient of The Chance The Rapper and Social Works, Computer Science Grant and implements computer science in head start through eighth grades. In addition to small group instruction and common core based instruction, Tanner implements social emotional learning in all classrooms. We support student learning through restorative practices, peace circles, peer jury, and talking circles. Students learn emotional intelligence, conflict resolution, self- advocacy, goal setting, and relationship building through a comprehensive social emotional culture supported by many community partnerships.

As a neighborhood school serving students in grades Pre-K through third grade, we are committed to fostering an environment where every child is known, supported, and challenged to reach their fullest potential.

At Jackie Robinson, our dedicated teachers integrate 21st-century instructional practices across literacy, mathematics, science, social studies, fine arts, health, and physical education. Beyond academics, we place a strong emphasis on social-emotional learning, character development, and goal-setting to help students build the confidence and skills they need to thrive both in school and in life.

We are proud of our partnerships with New Community Outreach and Accepted Admissions, which help us strengthen connections with our families and community. Together, we work to create a supportive, inclusive, and enriching environment that prepares our scholars to become leaders of tomorrow.
Thank you for being a part of the Jackie Robinson family. We look forward to partnering with you to ensure the success of every child in our school

Introduction:
Welcome to Dulles Elementary — Home of the Tigers!

I’m Principal Pullum, and I couldn’t be prouder to serve this incredible community of scholars, families, and educators. Every day, I walk through our doors knowing that Dulles is more than just a school — it’s a family built on purpose, passion, and possibility. From our littlest learners to our middle school leaders, we are shaping young minds to dream boldly, act bravely, and show up every day as true Goal-Getters.

This year, our theme isn’t just a slogan — it’s a mindset. Being a Goal-Setter means we name what we want, we make a plan, and we stay disciplined until we see it through. It’s about growth — academic, emotional, and personal. It’s about believing that effort beats excuses and that every challenge is an opportunity to rise higher.

At Dulles, we set goals that stretch us. We believe in the power of community, the strength of consistency, and the joy of seeing our students reach new heights. Our staff are committed to delivering rigorous instruction, building strong relationships, and keeping learning at the center of everything we do.

To our parents and families — thank you for being our partners in this journey. To our scholars — remember: your goals are the gateway to your greatness. Let’s make this year one of unstoppable growth, pride, and achievement.

Together, we are Dulles Strong.
Together, we are Goal-Getters.

— Principal Pullum
Proud Leader of Dulles Elementary School

Introduction:
Greetings McCutcheon Community!
It is truly an honor and privilege to become a part of the John T. McCutcheon STEAM Community. McCutcheon is a unique place, and I look forward to our journey together. 
I come to you, as a wife, and a mother of three, my oldest son is in banking, my daughter attends the University of Notre Dame, and my youngest son is a 5th-grade student in Chicago Public Schools. I have 27 years of experience as a primary teacher leader, instructional coach, assistant principal, and now your principal. I spent 18 years as a Kindergarten – 3rd-grade teacher and instructional coach and the past 8 years as assistant principal. I have had the privilege of serving diverse communities on the south and west sides of Chicago and now I am able to serve the Uptown community. 
I have a strong philosophical belief that all students deserve a safe, equitable, rigorous, and culturally relevant learning experience, infused with social-emotional support in all subject areas. Education has been a major pillar in my life and has driven me to advocate for students who have been traditionally underrepresented and underserved.
I believe in the unique partnerships and bonds that are developed through building strong and trusting relationships. My plan is to work closely with all stakeholders, LSC, school staff, students, and parents to continue to build on the great legacy of McCutcheon STEAM School. My conversations with staff, students, and district leadership have brought great insight into the core beliefs and values that have made McCutcheon into what it is today. I am committed to always exploring new ways to meet the needs of all students and actively support teachers’ practice. 
I am a hands-on leader, and I will continue to immerse myself into the McCutcheon community in order to ensure that students and staff are successful-because we are bound for greatness! 
In closing, please know that my door is always open to you. I welcome your conversation and input. Let us always keep our students as the primary focus of our work. I look forward to celebrating our collective successes in the years to come. 
 Sincerely, 
Kahinde Longmire, Principal

Introduction:
The Velma F. Thomas Early Childhood Center is a CPS Dual Language, Reggio-inspired preschool in the McKinley Park community.  We use a constructivist approach to teaching and learning which emphasizes an arts-based, child-driven curriculum, discovery and exploration.  Caregiver involvement in the child's preschool development is integral to the program.

We are rated an ISBE "Award of Excellence in Preschool Teaching and Learning" and a CPS "Arts Excelling" school.

Our families are primarily Latine, serving general education and students with disabilities. We have five blended and two instructional classrooms. Of the seven classrooms, we offer three half-day programs for 3-year old children and four full-day programs for 4-year old children.

Introduction:
Edison Park Elementary strives to provide a superior education that fosters critical thinking and independent learning while preparing students for college and career. We provide our students with differentiated instruction while creating challenging learning experiences in a safe environment. Our focus on rigorous academics instills a sense of shared responsibilities, accountability, and social development. 

The school visioin is "EPE is a positive, purposeful, productive community for all," and, over the last few years, we have done a lot of work around our three school priorities: 1) K - 8 aligned curriculum, 2) student support (both academically and behaviorally), and 3) grading practices. You will notice that our WOLF expectations (Winning Attitude, Own your choices, Leadership, Focus on respect) encompass all of our priorities as a school, which is, ultimately, doing what is best for our students. The students are purposely located in the center of our priorities as a reminder that they are the reason we do what we do.

Introduction: Welcome to Marvin Camras Children's Engineering School! We are proud to be a STEM and Leader in Me school, dedicated to nurturing bilingual leaders and empowering students to thrive academically, socially, and emotionally. At Camras, we are committed to delivering high-quality, student-centered instruction that prepares our students to engage in real world problem solving. We infuse our different curriculums (Eureka Math, ARC, Expedition Learning ELA,  Skyline Science and Social Studies) with Project Based Learning. This helps provide hands-on, engaging learning experiences that inspire critical thinking, real world problem solving, creativity, and collaboration.   At Camras, we strive to build strong partnerships with families and the community to ensure every child’s success. Together, we cultivate a supportive environment where every student is embraced and empowered to lead, learn, and grow. Welcome to our Camras familia!

Introduction:
Welcome to Sadlowski Elementary's Principal Corner

I'm thrilled to open my 7th year leading Sadlowski Elementary for the 2025-2026 school year! This is our 10th anniversary, and our theme is "Season 10"—a celebration of our dedication.

I’m incredibly proud of our progress, including our new designation as a dual language school and substantial gains in IAR scores and attendance. Our vision is an inclusive Pre-K to 8th grade community where every child thrives, with parents as vital partners.

Season 10 Focus: Our priorities are leveraging our dual language status, enhancing academic achievement, and supporting student well-being. We will implement rigorous curriculum and continue to address absenteeism. Our goals include improving 5Essentials scores, boosting student performance, and ensuring students in Tier 2 and Tier 3 receive targeted interventions.

Your partnership is crucial as we embark on "Sadlowski's Next Level." We are dedicated to transparent communication and creating opportunities for involvement so every Saber can succeed.

Please don't hesitate to reach out.

Principal Jimenez
--
Bienvenidos al Rincón del Director de la Primaria Sadlowski

¡Estoy encantado de comenzar mi 7.º año al frente de Sadlowski en este año escolar 2025-2026! Este es nuestro décimo aniversario, y nuestro tema es "Temporada 10"—una celebración de nuestro impulso y dedicación.

Estoy increíblemente orgulloso del progreso, incluida nuestra nueva designación como una escuela de lenguaje dual y avances sustanciales en resultados del IAR y la asistencia. Nuestra visión es una comunidad inclusiva de Pre-K a 8.º grado donde cada niño prospere, con los padres como socios vitales.

Enfoque Temporada 10: Nuestras prioridades son aprovechar nuestro estatus de lenguaje dual, mejorar el rendimiento académico y apoyar el bienestar estudiantil. Implementaremos un currículo riguroso y continuaremos abordando el ausentismo. Nuestros objetivos incluyen mejorar las puntuaciones de 5Essentials, impulsar el rendimiento estudiantil, y asegurar que los estudiantes en los niveles 2 y 3 reciban las intervenciones específicas que necesitan.

Su colaboración es crucial mientras nos embarcamos en "El Próximo Nivel de Sadlowski." Estamos dedicados a la comunicación transparente y a crear oportunidades de participación para que cada estudiante pueda tener éxito.

Por favor, no duden en comunicarse.

Director Jiménez

At Prieto Academy, we are committed to delivering high-quality, student-centered instruction that prepares our scholars to excel in a dynamic, global society. Our innovative curriculum includes Eureka Math Squared using the Teaching Math Through Problem Solving methodology, Skyline Spanish and English Language Arts, Writing Across the Curriculum, and Skyline Science. These programs provide hands-on, engaging learning experiences that inspire critical thinking, creativity, and collaboration. At Prieto, we strive to build strong partnerships with families and the community to ensure every child’s success. Together, we cultivate a supportive environment where every scholar is empowered to lead, learn, and grow. Thank you for visiting our page—welcome to our Prieto family!

Programs.ProgramOverview:
This program provides a comprehensive general education curriculum across all core academic subjects, with a focus on Fine & Performing Arts as an enriching complement to the standard coursework. Arts teachers in Fine & Performing Arts schools work with students and other classroom teachers to provide intensive and integrated instruction in the arts. Students are exposed to various arts opportunities and environments, and have the opportunity to learn and grow in multiple art forms: dance, drama, media arts, music, and/or visual arts.

Personalized learning is a learner-driven instructional model that fosters 21st century skills by empowering every student to actively co-design their learning path, pace, and environment according to their individual needs, strengths, and interests. Simply put, at the core of personalized learning is learner agency.

Introduction:
Kipling is a vibrant learning community where students are nurtured, challenged, and empowered to reach their full potential. Here, every child’s strengths are recognized, their voices are valued, and their growth is celebrated.

At Kipling, our commitment is to create a school environment where teachers are supported, students are active participants in their learning, and the school reflects both excellence and creativity. From classrooms to hallways, every space is designed to make students feel welcomed, proud, and inspired.

We prioritize strong relationships, high expectations, and a safe, inclusive environment. Our students, families, and community members work together to help every child’s potential shine.

Whether you are a current Kipling family, a prospective parent, or a community partner, we invite you to connect with us and be part of our journey. Kipling is a school on the rise — and we’re rising together!

PrekSchoolSummary:
Our preschool program supports early learning through a play-based and inquiry-driven approach that promotes curiosity, independence, and a love of learning. Teachers use the district-adopted Creative Curriculum to guide development across all key domains, including cognitive, social-emotional, language, and physical skills. Children engage in hands-on activities, collaborative projects, and structured routines that help them build problem-solving abilities, self-regulation, and positive peer interactions.

Introduction:
Rodolfo Lozano Bilingual and International Center is a neighborhood Magnet school serving students from Pre-K through 8th grade, offering a wide range of opportunities and services to support every child's growth and success. We are home to an early childhood program, cluster program and Spanish World Language. 
Lozano is a close-knit, dedicated community where children are empowered to thrive through a variety of in-school and after-school programs. Our classrooms are centered around a high-quality curriculum, ensuring that every student has access to the best education, regardless of the program they are in. We take great pride in our commitment to the Arts, with a full-time visual arts program and an Arts Liaison. We collaborate with renowned organizations like the Joffrey Ballet, Tiny Tunemakers, CHIME Music Therapy, and more to enrich our students' experiences.
We believe in supporting the whole child, providing wraparound services that include access to a full-time counselor and social worker. Our array of after-school enrichment programs, including sports, academic tutoring, yearbook club and aftercare, allow students to explore and develop their unique interests.
At Lozano, we foster a joyful, inclusive environment where all students are valued and encouraged to reach their fullest potential.
