Through strong partnerships with parents, community organizations, cultural institutions, universities, and corporations, we create enriching opportunities that enhance learning and personal growth.

Introduction:
Dear Families, Staff, and Community Partners,

As we reflect on our progress and look ahead, I am filled with gratitude for the students, families, and staff who make our school such a special place. Our work is grounded in a shared commitment to nurturing every child’s social, emotional, and academic growth—because learning happens best when children feel safe, supported, and connected.

We believe every student deserves to be seen, heard, and valued. Teachers greet students by name each morning, setting a positive tone that reinforces belonging. Our focus on academic excellence means maintaining high expectations and providing the support needed to meet them.

Teachers are bringing our new Eureka Math² curriculum to life through lessons that promote discussion and problem-solving. In literacy, students read diverse texts and write for authentic purposes, developing as critical thinkers and communicators. Formative assessments guide instruction and ensure every child gets the support they need.

Behind each powerful classroom experience is a teacher who is continually learning. Through collaborative learning cycles, our educators reflect, plan, and improve practice to drive student growth. Our student support team—counselors, social workers, and interventionists—ensures that every child has an advocate and a plan for success.

Family partnership remains essential. Together, we create the conditions for learning both in school and at home. Your trust, insights, and collaboration strengthen our collective impact.

The state of our school is strong—not because we have finished growing, but because we grow together. Thank you for being part of this journey.

Chicago Public Schools (CPS) is reimagining our approach to accountability, emphasizing the holistic development of students. This means focusing not only on academic success but also on students' growth and well-being. We are working hard to fully implement our new approach by Fall 2025. This will be done in stages to give our schools and stakeholders time to understand changes and receive ongoing support. For more information, visit cps.edu/CIDT.
OverallRatingDescription: Per Chicago Board of Education policy, district-managed schools are assigned an annual school accountability status in order to identify schools on remediation or probation.
ClassificationDescription: Schools that have an attendance boundary. Generally, all students who live within this area may attend the school. Acceptance based on student living in boundary area or application if out of boundary area.
ProgramsSummer: Bike The Lake Front, Deejaying 101, Explore your Inner Artist, Play and Write Exploration, Soccer Fitness, Stay Cool and Play Chess, Summer Jammin Rock Band
StudentGrowthDescription: Student Growth measures the change in standardized test scores between two points in time. This growth is compared to the average national growth for schools that started in the same place. A 50th percentile score means the school grew at the same rate as the national average.
PrekSchoolSummary: Our preschool program boosts academic skills through a play-based and inquiry-based approach which helps foster independence, prepares students for kindergarten, and instills a lifelong love of learning. Teachers utilize a district-wide curriculum, the Creative Curriculum, to provide support for student learning and development across all essential areas including social emotional skills. To ensure all students have the opportunity to engage in high-quality early learning experiences, preschool programs are offered free of charge.

Introduction:
Welcome to Gresham School of Excellence and SY27! I am proud and passionate about continuing to serve our scholars, the Auburn Gresham Community and Partners. I look forward to this school year and am hopeful that this website provides you with relevant, timely, and useful information about the many exciting programs and events, to create a rich and vibrant learning experience for our scholars.

Over the past four years, our scholars have made tremendous academic gains, across all content areas. This school year we will continue our efforts to improve student achievement through implementing a high quality curriculum, acceleration and intentional tiered interventions. Our teachers will continue to receive instructional coaching and embed data cycles in their weekly professional development, to meet our students where they are and sustain academic growth. In addition, our scholars will continue to receive a well rounded educational experience with access to after school enrichment and activities, to ensure all students are college and career ready.

Social emotional learning is another focus for us this school year. Our scholars will have voice and input on what their daily educational experience looks, sounds and feels like. Our scholars will engage daily in the second step tier one curriculum, which builds a foundation for a positive, inclusive culture through developing social-emotional competencies, which include perspective-taking, empathy, processing emotions, understanding and resolving conflicts, and building positive relationships. This is a critical part of our students' daily experience, as it teaches our scholars problem solving skills and how to successfully express their feelings.

Sincerely,

Mr. Twomey

Introduction:
Located in the vibrant Pullman community on the South Side of Chicago, Wendell Smith Elementary School is a cornerstone of the local educational landscape. Serving grades PK-8, the school is committed to providing a high-quality education that empowers students to excel academically, socially, and emotionally. Wendell Smith strives to create a learning environment that celebrates diversity, fosters academic achievement, and supports the development of the whole child.

Our dedicated team of educators and staff work collaboratively to create a nurturing atmosphere where students are challenged to reach their full potential. Through innovative instructional practices, a focus on personalized learning, and strong community engagement, we aim to develop critical thinkers, effective communicators, and compassionate citizens. Wendell Smith offers a variety of programs, including a robust afterschool initiative, STEAM-focused events, and a commitment to ensuring all students have access to the tools and resources they need for success.

As part of our ongoing commitment to improvement, Wendell Smith is actively working to enhance teacher professional development, implement data-driven instructional strategies, and build stronger partnerships with families and the community. With a strong emphasis on SEL (social-emotional learning) and an unwavering dedication to equity, Wendell Smith is working to shape future leaders who will thrive both inside and outside the classroom.

SchoolLongName: Gerald Delgado Kanoon Elementary Magnet School
Introduction:
Gerald Delgado Kanoon Magnet Elementary School is a vibrant Pre-K–8 learning community committed to academic excellence, cultural pride, and student voice. Kanoon provides rigorous, high-quality curriculum that develops biliterate, critical thinkers prepared to lead in a global society.

Through collaborative Learning Cycles, Rigor Walks, and data-driven planning, teachers create classrooms where students engage in meaningful teaming, academic discourse, and authentic problem-solving. Our instructional focus on Curriculum & Instruction and Connectedness & Well-Being ensures every child feels seen, supported, and challenged.

Kanoon’s success is strengthened by powerful community partnerships with organizations such as Sidley & Austin, Latinos Progresando, the Chicago Blackhawks,  and the Marshall Square Resource Network, which expand learning opportunities beyond the classroom through mentorship, enrichment, and family engagement initiatives.

Rooted in collaboration and a deep sense of belonging, Kanoon empowers students to take ownership of their learning, celebrate their heritage, and lead with purpose in their community and beyond.

New Approach to Supporting Student Development
Chicago Public Schools (CPS) is reimagining our approach to accountability, emphasizing the holistic development of students. This means focusing not only on academic success but also on students' growth and well-being. We are working hard to fully implement our new approach by Fall 2025. This will be done in stages to give our schools and stakeholders time to understand changes and receive ongoing support. For more information, visit cps.edu/CIDT.

StudentGrowthDescription: Student Growth measures the change in standardized test scores between two points in time. This growth is compared to the average national growth for schools that started in the same place. A 50th percentile score means the school grew at the same rate as the national average.
PrekSchoolSummary: Our preschool program boosts academic skills through a play-based and inquiry-based approach which helps foster independence, prepares students for kindergarten, and instills a lifelong love of learning. Teachers utilize a district-wide curriculum, the Creative Curriculum, to provide support for student learning and development across all essential areas including social emotional skills. To ensure all students have the opportunity to engage in high-quality early learning experiences, preschool programs are offered free of charge.

SchoolLongName: Walter Henri Dyett High School for the Arts
Introduction: Welcome to our school where every student’s story matters, and every dream has room to grow. We are a vibrant learning community committed to nurturing the whole child through meaningful relationships, rigorous instruction, and a culture of belonging. From dynamic instruction and engaging clubs to targeted supports and strong partnerships with families, our work is rooted in helping every student thrive academically, socially, and personally. Our classrooms are alive with curiosity, creativity, and opportunities for students to explore who they are and who they aspire to become. From academic excellence to social-emotional growth, we are proud to offer experiences that empower students to thrive today and lead tomorrow. We’re honored to share the many things that make our school a special place to learn, grow, and shine. Whether it’s in the classroom, on the stage, in the lab, or on the field, students are encouraged to discover their strengths and pursue their purpose. We are proud to be a school where potential becomes achievement and where learners become leaders. For our students—today and always, Dori Butler, Principal

Introduction:
Situated in the Rogers Park neighborhood, Sullivan High School is a tight-knit public institution dedicated to serving our community. Our student body is exceptionally diverse, speaking numerous languages, and we foster a supportive, inclusive environment that celebrates cultural intersection. 
We are committed to preparing students for life beyond graduation through rigorous, innovative coursework. This includes a strong early college partnership with the City Colleges of Chicago, an expanding array of Advanced Placement offerings, and specialized Career and Technical Education pathways in Medical and Business. Beyond academic excellence, Sullivan graduates emerge as empathetic, equity-minded leaders equipped with the essential relationship-building skills to make a tangible impact.

Introduction: William Howard Taft High School, one of the city’s largest public high schools, spans two campuses: the Freshman Academy (grades 7–9) and Varsity Campus (grades 10–12). As an IB World School, it offers the MYP, DP, and CP Programmes, along with AP, dual-credit courses, and NJROTC. Taft provides over 100 clubs, 75 teams, and 34 varsity sports, promoting academic, artistic, and athletic growth. Guided by its mission, “Educating Global Citizens to Create a Better World,” Taft fosters excellence, diversity, and inclusion. Recognized as a "Best High School" by U.S. News & World Report for six consecutive years, Taft inspires success.

SchoolLongName: Edward Tilden Career Community Academy HS
Introduction: Tilden high school is a school on the rise that's currently home to approximately 250 students. As a neighborhood high school, students do not have to meet criteria for acceptance other than residing in Tilden's attendance area. This means, students do not have to take any assessments or participate in any school lottery for admittance. Over the past few years, Tilden has focused on its high school graduation rate and increase of ECCC opportunities for students. In SY24, the 4 year graduation rate increased by 5.5%, the 5 year graduation rate increased by 7.3%, and ECCC increased by 14.8%. Additionally, the college enrollment rate increased by 2.5%. A unique aspect of Tilden high school is the 4x4 Block Schedule. Tilden students take 4 classes per semester and earn 1 full credit at the end of the semester. This college-like structure allows students to earn 8 credits per year instead of 7 at other schools. Additionally, students have more room in their schedule to take AP courses, Dual Credit Courses, or participate in work-study programs.

Introduction:
Percy L. Julian High School is one of nine high schools serving the Far South Side. Julian is a neighborhood school, however many students who do not live in attendance area enroll in the school to participate in our Career Technical Education Programs: Business, Gaming, Radio TV Broadcast, Medical Academy, and Digital Media. This year we will be adding JROTC for students interested in a leadership pathway. 

Julian is rated strong in the arts.  Recognitions have been received for the outstanding work of the Radio-TV Broadcasting Academy and Marching Band. The grade-level interdisciplinary service-learning program has received national recognition from the Education Commission of the States. Students have opportunities to participate in a variety of extra-curricular activities.  The support and engagement of community partners, including alumni, working with the school is strong.  

Percy L. Julian High School has been awarded accreditation by the North Central Association Commission on Accreditation and School Improvement, the Northwest Accreditation Commission and the Southern Association of Colleges and Schools Commission on Accreditation and School Improvement. SchoolLongName: Roberto Clemente Community Academy High School
Introduction:
Roberto Clemente Community Academy is a wall-to-wall International Baccalaureate World school that develops students through intercultural understanding with an emphasis on critical thinking.  Our curricula is aligned with the IB pedagogical framework as well as the Common Core State Standards. Both are designed to prepare students to contribute productively to their local, national, and global communities. Students can participate in the IB Diploma Programme, Career-related Programme, and Middle Years Programme. Additional pathways include career education in Allied Health, Broadcast Technology, or Culinary Arts.
As a comprehensive neighborhood school, Clemente also offers athletics and extracurricular activities.  Our campus features 3 music rooms, 3 fine arts rooms, 2 gymnasiums, a weight room, athletic fields, and newly remodeled science labs. Clemente's renovated Media Center contains a film lab, audio recording studio, and a Mac lab. In order to prepare our students to compete in college and the career marketplace, Clemente provides over 450 devices to support student learning: 8 hardwired labs, 5 mobile labs, 30 SMART board classrooms, tablets, and laptops.

SchoolLongName: Ellen H Richards Career Academy High School
Introduction:
Richards Career Academy (RCA)...where every Student is Known, Valued, and Inspired.  RCA offers 2 award-winning Career & Technical Education (CTE) programs -- Culinary Arts and Business/Entrepreneurship.  Due to the unique 4x4 Block schedule, students have an opportunity to earn 8 credits per school year and more options in their schedule for Early College coursework and opportunities.  With more than 12 after-school Clubs, and 11 + Athletics Teams there is something for everyone at RCA!
As 1 of 20 Sustainable Community Schools (SCS) in CPS, RCA embraces the SCS movement to create radical change and success for young people, their families, and the community.  Thriving at RCA looks like living out the 6 Pillars of SCS: 1) Curricula that are culturally relevant, engaging, and challenging; 2) High Quality Teaching; 3) Wrap Around Supports; 4) Restorative Justice and Social-Emotional Learning Development; 5) Authentic Engagement of Parents, Family, & Community; 6) Inclusive School Leadership.  
Richards is the host site for the Back of the Yards Parent University where parents and families can access a wide variety of services and educational programs.

Introduction:
Morgan Park High School is one of Chicago’s premier Neighborhood & International Baccalaureate High Schools.  Founded in 1916, Morgan Park has produced generations of proud Mustang graduates, who have gone on to achieve professional and personal successes locally, statewide, and nationally.

As an International Baccalaureate World School with 1,200 students and 150 staff members, Morgan Park prides itself in its three core IB Programs:

  • IB Middle Years Program: a curriculum rooted in inquiry, to challenge students of all interests and academic abilities in Grades 7-10.  
  • IB Diploma and Career-Related Programmes are selective, advanced-level college preparatory programmes designed to help students transition into college with the skills and knowledge they need to succeed.

Additionally, Morgan Park offers a spectrum of Advanced Placement, Dual Credit, and Honors courses.  Nearly 200 cadets are enrolled in Morgan Park High School’s robust JROTC program, pairing their JROTC experience with the academic programs above.

Morgan Park is committed to educating the whole student; this commitment extends to investing in high-quality, robust extracurricular programs.  Morgan Park currently offers 25+ extracurricular programs, including Robotics, Marching Band, Theatre, Debate, and Yearbook.  Morgan Park’s Athletic Department, with a history of excellence across many sports, offers students access to 20+ IHSA sports programs per year.

Students can enroll at Morgan Park through four pathways:

  • Academic Center: Admission to this selective program is through GoCPS for 7th & 8th Grade students.
  • International Baccalaureate Cohort Students: Admission to this choice program is through GoCPS for 9th Grade students.
  • Special Education w/ Significantly Modified Curriculum: Admission to this choice program is through GoCPS for 9th Grade students.
  • Neighborhood Students: Admission is open to students living in Morgan Park’s Attendance Area.

Go Mustangs!

Welcome to the 2026–2027 school year!

I am proud to welcome our students, families, and community to another school year at Wendell Phillips High School. At Phillips, we are committed to providing a strong daily learning experience while preparing every student for life beyond high school.

This year, our work is centered on two priorities that guide everything we do.

Effective Instruction

We are strengthening what happens in every classroom, every day. Students will engage in grade level content, think critically, and produce high quality work that shows their understanding. Our focus is on clear expectations, strong teaching, and consistent learning experiences so all students grow and achieve.

Postsecondary Success

We are ensuring students have clear pathways after graduation. This includes access to rigorous courses, career exploration, and real world experiences that prepare them for college, careers, and other opportunities. Every student will leave Phillips with a plan and the skills to take their next step with confidence.

Our work is grounded in our 3 Es: Excellence, Effectiveness, and Efficiency, which guide how we teach, lead, and support our school community each day. We are also proud of our strong partnerships with colleges and universities, workforce and career organizations, and community-based partners that expand opportunities, provide resources, and meet the diverse needs of our students.

We believe in our students, we believe in our community, and we are committed to building a school where strong daily learning leads to powerful futures. As a proud part of the Bronzeville community, Phillips continues to serve as a cornerstone for opportunity, growth, and excellence for our students and families.

Rashad Talley, Principal

Introduction:
Roosevelt High School is the neighborhood high school of Albany Park, one of Chicago’s most diverse communities. Our families and staff celebrate this diversity in our Dual Language program, one of only 3 dual language high schools in Chicago. In addition, we have 5 highly successful Career Pathway programs (CTE) which draw students from across the city, including IT/Networking, IT, Game Design and Coding, Health Careers, Culinary Arts and the Education Pathway for students excited to become teachers themselves one day.

Roosevelt has an extensive arts program, including visual fine arts, photography, digital design, band performance, vocal performance and drama. 

We boast a brand new turf soccer field, home to boys and girls, soccer, football, flag football, softball and baseball. Our two gyms host boys/girls volleyball, badminton, and boys/girls basketball.Our top quality pool supports our swim and water polo teams

Roosevelt has one of the largest after school club programs in Chicago, including Latin Dance, Student Writers, Spirit Club, Student Voice, Martial Arts, Gender

Introduction:
At Wells, our vision for young people is that all students are critically thinking, creative, empathetic change-makers who commit to their own growth and development within their local community and our global society.

To achieve that vision, we work to prepare young people for success after high school by placing equal value on high-quality, rigorous education and social-emotional wellness. As a fine arts academy, we recognize that centering student voice and creativity drives excellence and therefore we elevate the arts and arts-based initiatives in our teaching and learning.

Each day, Wells students also seek to display the characteristics of our R.I.S.E. principles: Respect, Integrity, Self-Expression, and Engagement.

Introduction:
William J. Bogan is an approved International Baccalaureate school.  The school hosts the MYP for All program for 9th and 10th grade students.  The student also host the Diploma Programme for select 11th and 12th grade students, CTE Entrepreneurship and Accounting, and offers opportunities for dual enrollment at Daley. 

Bogan is Chicago Public School's first1:1 High School.  The school integrates technology to support inquiry, academic achievement, and the development of the IB Learner Profile.

The school has several notable teachers and leaders - 3 CPS Ones to Watch (technology integration), a CPS Framework Specialist (instructional excellence), an author of the state civics curriculum, an Urban STEM fellow, and 2 NBTC teachers.

Students who attend Bogan have the opportunity to participate in a variety of extra-curricular activities from academic clubs like Debate or Anime to award winning athletic teams.

Our school's vision is "Excellence Today, Success Tomorrrow: Bogan Today, College Tomorrow".  We are focused on helping students build their College Selectivity and becoming independent learners.

To empower every student to achieve more.

Vision Statement
To change the game of school through support, opportunities, and instruction.

Core Values: 
Perseverance: We keep working until we're successful. 
Respect: We treat others the way we want to be treated. 
Integrity: We do what’s right. 
Decorum: We act in decency and order. 
Excellence: We are capable of doing more so aim high.

CIWP Goals SY24-26
- 30% of students will earn a 3.0 or higher GPA
- 90% Freshman On-Track rate 
- 80% Sophomore On-Track rate
- 90% attendance rate 
- 80% of students will be in the Blue or Green

Introduction: Welcome to Kelvyn Park Junior and Senior High School! I’m Michelle Suttmeier, and I am proud to serve as the principal of this vibrant learning community located in the heart of Chicago’s Hermosa neighborhood on the city’s northwest side. At Kelvyn Park, we serve students in grades 7–12 and are dedicated to fostering creativity, curiosity, and academic excellence. As a Fine and Performing Arts school, we celebrate the power of artistic expression while preparing students for the future through access to early college coursework and a wide range of enrichment opportunities. Our goal is to ensure every student graduates confident, capable, and ready to thrive in college, career, and life.

Introduction:
Ogden International is the only full continuum preK-12 public International Baccalaureate school in the State of Illinois, and only one of 25 in North America. Ogden is also one of the ten most diverse schools in the Chicago Public School District, serving the downtown area with families from foreign consulates and global corporations choosing to enroll at Ogden.

An Ogden International School education engages a K-12 diverse student body with inquiry-based learning experiences fostering empathy, critical thinking and global mindedness for the world of tomorrow. Ogden International’s globally-recognized IB programmes provide concept-based, academic frameworks, and student centered learning by inquiry grounded in global context and real life situations.

Through internationally-based learning opportunities, Ogden aims to develop leaders who possess the intellectual, emotional and social skills to live, learn and work in a rapidly globalizing world.

Introduction:
Englewood STEM High School opened in fall 2019 starting with an inaugural freshman class. The school is housed in a brand new, state-of-the-art facility, which includes world-class multipurpose educational spaces, a modern outdoor sports facility, and a school-based medical center for use by both students as well as community residents.

Englewood STEM High School has added one grade each subsequent year until it serves grades 9-12 beginning in school year 2022-23. The school is a neighborhoodEarly College Science, Technology, Engineering, and Math (STEM) High School, where every classroom will be designed to develop students into knowledgeable, flexible, resourceful problem solvers.

Through a unique collaboration that connects high school, college, and career,Englewood STEM High School is paired with Kennedy-King College (KKC) andSalesforce, which provides real-world experience and prepares students for high-demand careers in science and technology.

Students will have the option to earn college credit through KKC, leading to an associate degree, an advanced certificate, or a basic certificate while in high school.Students can also get hands-on career experience and earn certifications through Career Technical Education (CTE) Pathways in Information Technology (IT) and Health Sciences. Salesforce will provide valuable enrichment opportunities, such as internships, mentoring, and other work-based learning experiences. Through these programs, students will graduate uniquely prepared to succeed in STEM careers, while their early college and career credentials will give them a head-start toward completing their degree.

Introduction: Back of the Yards College Preparatory High School is an International Baccalaureate World School located in the historic Back of the Yards community. Application for admission to the school is required for all students who are interested in attending; Freshmen and sophomore students engage in the Middle Years Program (MYP) and may select the appropriate IB path in their junior and senior years, including the International Baccalaureate Diploma Programme (DP) or the International Baccalaureate Career Programme (CP). Back of the Yards College Prep offers students a wide variety of after school opportunities, including athletics and clubs. Students are highly encouraged to engage in any of the after school options as an integral part of their learning and high school experience.

Introduction:
Welcome to Douglass Academy High School—The Jewel of the Westside, proudly rooted in the Austin community. At Douglass, we provide a close-knit, small-school environment where every student is known by name. This personal connection allows us to shape a positive narrative for our students—one that empowers them to rise above the challenges they may encounter outside our walls.

Our educators deliver explicit instruction in positive character development, supported by clear and consistent behavioral expectations that guide students toward success. We are committed to nurturing both the academic and social growth of every learner.

Douglass Academy offers a Comprehensive Student Supports Program, staffed to meet the unique needs of our diverse student population. Through our two-teacher instructional model, students receive targeted Tier 1 and Tier 2 supports within the general education classroom. Additional small-group and individualized interventions are provided for students who may enter below grade level or face academic challenges.

Our dedicated team of stakeholders works collaboratively to design individualized support plans that ensure each student receives the tools, guidance, and encouragement needed to thrive.

Upon graduation, Douglass Academy students are equipped with the academic skills, social competencies, and confidence necessary to become productive and responsible citizens.

Douglass Academy High School—The Jewel of the Westside, where failure is not an option.

At GWCP, we commit to providing high quality learning experiences.  Our dedicated faculty and staff are here to support and inspire every student to reach their full potential.  We offer diverse and rigorous academic programs, extracurricular activities and support services designed to foster excellence, perseverance, integrity, curiosity and kindness, we call the Warrior Way. 

Our school is not just a place for academic learning but a community where every student is valued. We believe in nurturing the whole student – academically, socially, and emotionally. We encourage you to explore our website to learn more about the exciting opportunities awaiting you. From our rigorous academic programs to our array of clubs and sports teams, there is something for everyone at George Westinghouse College Prep High School. Be sure to stay connected through our calendar of events, news updates, and social media channels.

Introduction:
Lindblom, a US News & World Report Gold Medal School, offers high-achieving students unique programs in critical world languages, math and science. With the largest Mandarin language program in Chicago and the largest non-heritage Arabic program in the United States, our language program affords students unique and rich opportunities.

Our Biotechnology Center of Excellence, run in partnership with Baxter International and the Office of STEM Education Partnerships at Northwestern University, provides the anchor for our deep STEM program. 

We offer three CTE program strands:

Computer Networking, Game Programming, and Web Dev/Design

Pre-Engineering

Teaching Academy

.

Lindblom graduates have included Posse scholarship winners, a QuestBridge recipient, and Gates Scholars. Our Class of 2025 earned over $96 million in verified scholarships!

Lindblom is the #1 school for College Enrollment.

Lindblom is Ranked #11 in the state of Illinois by US News & World Reports.

Lindblom is Ranked #7 in Chicagoland by Chicago Magazine.

SchoolLongName: South Shore Intl College Prep High School
Introduction:
Welcome to South Shore International College Prep where our scholars are anchored in excellence! At SSICP we think critically, write purposefully, and apply learning in real-world situations to prepare scholars for post-secondary excellence as leaders who will impact their local and global communities. Our school prepares all students for success as internationally minded scholars who approach all facets of life with excellence. As TARS, our students are Tenacious | Anchored in Excellence| Responsible| Scholars.

At South Shore International College Prep, we offer a highly competitive personalized high school experience with all of our scholars participating in the International Baccalaureate programmes. 9th grade scholars enter our school as Middle Years Programme participants culminating in a Personal Project in their sophomore year which demonstrates their learning and research skills in a project focused on their personal passion. At the end of their sophomore year, scholars choose their post-secondary preparatory pathway as a Business, Medical and Health Careers, Career-Related Programme or Diploma Programme scholar. 

All juniors and seniors take college level course work and take exams at the end of their senior year which translate into college credit. To date, over 74% of our seniors have graduated with enough college credits to cover at least one college course and 39% of scholars have credit for two or more college courses. Record numbers of our scholars have also received the prestigious Gates and Posse scholarships as a result of their academic achievements.

Beyond academics, our student body and energetic staff are highly engaged as members of the global community. We are committed to exposing each student to varied levels of Internationalism, from studying various cultures to international communications to world travel. Our scholars have traveled to Costa Rica, China, Ecuador, England, France, and Peru to name a few locations! We are committed to at least one global experience per year that is open to our entire school community.

In addition to globalism, our scholars show excellence in athletics where our scholar athletes ranked 2nd in State for Girls Track in 2024 and our Football team was 7 and 3 in 2025 with a matchup with Metamora HS in the playoffs! In addition to sports, our scholars rank 1st in the country in academic competitions through our Medical Program (HOSA) and our Business program (FBLA).

SchoolLongName: Mary E Courtenay Elementary Language Arts Center
Introduction:
Courtenay Language Arts Center is a neighborhood school located in the Uptown neighborhood.  We prioritize an education for students focused on the whole child through building critical thinking, collaboration, and discourse skills. 

Courtenay is rated Strong in the Creative Schools Certification for the Arts, offers a Gold Level PreK program, K-8th grade classrooms, and classrooms offering Significantly Modified Curriculum w/ Moderate Supports.  At Courtenay, we offer students an inclusive environment with a focus on Core Curriculum in Reading, Math, Science, Social Studies, and Social-Emotional Learning.  Our students have daily classes focused on music, visual arts, physical education, or performing arts.  Courtenay offers 1:1 technology using iPads/Chromebooks.  All of our K-5th grade and Cluster (K-8th) classrooms are equipped with Promethean Boards.  

In addition to our classroom spaces, we have a Curiosity Classroom donated by the Children’s Museum of Chicago, a Snoozelen Room offering sensory experiences for students, a science lab, a NEW playground with universal access, auditorium, gymnasium, separate cafeteria, and more!  

Our after school programming offers students a variety of academic and enrichment programs free to families including English as a Second Language, Dance, sport programming, and rotating additional classes by quarter.

We have partnerships with Community in Schools, University of Illinois, YOU Parent Workshops, Design Dance, Navy Pier Children’s Museum, Alternatives, Trellus Behavioral Health, Becoming A Man (BAM), and many others!

Please visit our website to schedule a tour of our amazing campus!

SchoolLongName: Calmeca Academy of Fine Arts and Dual Language
Introduction: Calmeca Academy provides rigorous instructional programs that support Common Core Standards, promote acquisition of learning a second/third language and supporting Fine Arts. Instruction is unique and innovative constantly utilizing research-based programs and strategies. Dual Language is implemented in Pre-K through 5th grade this year and will grow through the years until all students instructed in the Dual Language philosophy. Mandarin is taught to students in grades K to 8th grades. External partners include UIC, ISU, Univ. of Chicago, Columbia College, Old Town School of Music, Greater Chicago Food Depository, Mariachi Heritage Foundation, Illinois Youth Soccer, and Changing Worlds. Calmeca provides workshops and trainings for parents supporting a strong parent involvement program. The weekly Healthy Kids Market provides families with fresh fruits and vegetables for all families. Additionally, the school holds the Silver Level award for its efforts in promoting Healthy and Wellness programs and events for its students. The after school program provides students the opportunity to engage in sports, arts, and tutoring.

Introduction:
Ashburn Community School opened its doors ten years ago to relieve overcrowding in eight area schools on controlled enrollment. As a result, Ashburn is now culturally diverse and serves more than 400 students. Parents are encouraged to participate in the Local School Council (LSC), Parent Advisory Council (PAC), and Bilingual Advisory Council (BAC).

We know that as parents you have lots of choices, we hope you choose Ashburn. Ashburn offers a rigorous educational program, Fine and Performing Arts Curriculum, and Pre-Algebra and Algebra for selected students. Ashburn is a Personalized Learning School and we believe in student agency, voice, and choice. Our Motto is "Moving from Good to Exceptional” and we are dedicated and committed to ensuring the best educational experience for you and your child. We invite you to come and volunteer and see Ashburn at its best. We want you to take advantage of these offerings and make Ashburn your choice for an amazing elementary school experience!

SchoolLongName: Ida B Wells Preparatory Elementary Academy
Introduction:
Ida B. Wells Preparatory Academy Elementary School is a (PreK-8) International Baccalaureate World School and an  Apple Distinguished School of approximately 300 students. Wells Prep promotes global citizenship through international mindedness, international travels, service learning, cultural exchange programs, and culturally relevant curriculum. We have partnerships with Apple, University of Chicago Stem Education, Ada S McKinley, Chicago Youth Centers, HELP (Healing Education Learning Professionals), and CHI&SE. 

Wells Prep has a record and reputation of excellent student achievement and an appealing  school culture and climate. As a twenty-first century IB (International Baccalaureate) world school, we offer a rigorous and student- centered curriculum that educates the whole child while promoting problem solving skills needed to navigate today’s complex  problems. In partnership with CYC (Chicago Youth Centers) we offer robust academic and extracurricular programs (robotics, keyboarding, sewing, cooking, choir, theatre, ballet, African dance, band, bowling, chess, etc.) after school. 

Our student population is slowly becoming diverse as well. Due to continued changes in the community in recent years, we have seen a growing population of immigrant, Hispanic, and Caucasian families here at Wells Prep. We appreciate diversity and promote intercultural experiences – both of which have become the bedrock of culturally relevant and responsive curriculum in our classrooms. Cognitive student engagement and student discourse at Wells Prep is enriched and grounded in the diverse cultural perspectives and backgrounds of our students and staff. Every classroom selected a country upon which to ground its inquiry and discourse.

Mason Elementary School is a Pre-Kindergarten through 8th grade school servicing the North Lawndale area.  Our programs include a blended program for 4 year old students as well as an AM and PM component.  We are truly a community school.  The typical day ends at 5:00 PM.  This allows us to meet students' academic and social needs.  Mason school strives to welcome families in a family-centered environment.  Many of our students start in our pre-kindergarten program and remain with us until they complete the 8th grade.  We are a 21st Century Community School.  On average, our teachers have 20 years of experience in the educational field.  Mason is part of the Healthy Schools initiative.

Introduction:
At the heart of everything we do is one simple belief: when we lead with love, purpose, and high expectations, extraordinary things happen. Every day, we have the privilege of shaping not just minds, but futures. That begins with leading with our hearts.

Leading with heart means seeing the best in every child, believing in their potential, and creating a space where they feel seen, heard, and valued. It means extending grace and empathy, while also holding firm to the belief that every student deserves access to rigorous instruction that challenges and inspires them to think deeply and dream boldly.

Equity is not just a word we say but it’s the lens through which we teach, support, and make decisions. It means meeting each student where they are, removing barriers, and ensuring that every learner has the tools and opportunities they need to succeed.

And while we take learning seriously, we also know that school should be a place of joy. When students laugh, explore, and connect, they discover that learning can be both meaningful and fun. That joy is what fuels curiosity, creativity, and confidence which are all essential ingredients for lifelong success.

Ultimately, our mission is to prepare our students not only for college, but for life. To be thinkers, leaders, and changemakers who go into the world ready to make a difference.

Together, with heart, rigor, and joy, we’re building a community where every student can thrive.

Programs.ProgramOverview:
Advanced Placement for All. No Exceptions. Every Social Justice High School (SOJO) student takes Advanced Placement coursework — not a select few. All four years are vertically aligned around one throughline: Identity → Perspective → Justice → Action — culminating in the FIRE Project. SOJO was born from the Little Village and North Lawndale communities' desire to keep the hunger strike's values of peace and equity alive for every graduate. We prepare students for careers in civic leadership, environmental justice, law, community advocacy, the nonprofit sector, entrepreneurship, and other fields that students aspire to be leaders in. Our unique workforce development program supports a cohort of students to secure paid out-of-school jobs tied to attendance, plus mentorship and career exploration that turn class time into opportunity. Introduction:
Uplift Community High School is one of the first two Early College STEAM High Schools in Chicago. The school was established in 2005. Located on the shores of Lake Michigan, in the diverse Uptown neighborhood, students have the ability to learn in an environment and high school unlike any other. Our beautiful facility and campus is located just blocks from Harry S. Truman College, one of the City Colleges of Chicago, where students can take college level courses during the school day. Students have the opportunity to request a modified class schedule that enables them to earn both high school and college credit simultaneously. In fact, through our Early STEAM program, students at Uplift can earn their associates degree or significant credit toward completion before ever graduating high school!

Uplift offers pathways in the following areas:

Associate of Science, Environmentalism & Sustainability 
Associate of Art, Elementary Education
Associate of Art, Secondary Education 

Our school was founded on the principles of social justice and we seek to produce graduates who are well informed and who have the ability to impact their communities, our city, our nation and ultimately the world for the greater good of humanity. Uplift students are game changers and have left their mark in society.

Uplift is Uptown's Early College STEAM High School!

Introduction: Beard School is an Early Childhood Specialty School that stands out with its two interrelated programs on one vibrant campus. Our largest program is our preschool program.  We are located on the Northwest side of Chicago, offering a comprehensive range of full-day and half-day options for all eligible 3 and 4-year-old students. Here, we provide tailored learning experiences through our general education, blended, English Language Learner (ELL), and intensive support special education programs. Our preschool programs are designed to prepare students for kindergarten and have a Gold Circle of Quality rating from ExceleRate, reflecting our commitment to excellence in educational and social emotional standards.  Our second largest program is our Specialty School, Kindergarten through 3rd grade program.  This program is exclusively for students with disabilities.  These classrooms prioritize individualized educational support, social emotional, and academic learning.  Our school has an ADA-compliant environment and is staffed by experts trained in a multitude of disabilities, including autism, medical disorders, and mobility issues. With a maximum of 10 students per classroom, we maintain a low student-to-adult ratio to ensure personalized attention and instruction.  With a full team of related service providers, including Speech, Occupational, Physical Therapies, Social Work, Counseling, Case Management, Nursing, and Psychology services, students are offered comprehensive support to effectively address the diverse needs of their IEP's within a classroom setting.  At Beard School, we are committed to fostering a culture of high expectations for all students and strong level of parental partnership.

PrekSchoolSummary: Beard School serves as an intervention school for the district. With a specialization in Early Childhood and Special Education, we have two different programs to support students Preschool through 3rd grade on one beautiful campus. With one of the largest preschool programs on the Northwest side of Chicago, our preschool program services over 350 four year olds. Our Gold Circle of Quality rating from ExceleRate, Excelling rating in Fine Arts, and SEL and Restorative Practices designations from CPS reflect our commitment to excellence in educational standards. Our dedication to student achievement is strengthened through professional development for staff, service leadership, and collaboration with our families and the community.

PrekSchoolSummary: At Barbara Vick Early Childhood and Family Centers, we advocate for play as the cornerstone of learning. Our curriculum, centered around the child and driven by their interests, fosters a play-based approach. We view teachers and students as collaborators in the learning process, creating intentional environments that cultivate relationships, utilize thought-provoking materials, and foster an appreciation for the outdoors. Inspired by the core values of the Reggio Emilia philosophy, we recognize children’s “hundred languages” for communication and expression, evident in our environments and students’ interactions with classroom materials. Play, nature, and the arts serve as vehicles for expression, deepening children’s understanding of the world. Documentation plays a vital role, making children’s learning visible.  By providing diverse materials, we open doors to varied learning experiences for both learners and staff. Inclusivity is paramount. We support families, encouraging active participation in their child’s education, fostering a community where everyone, regardless of individual needs, can thrive.
